To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intramyocardial delivery (IM) of bFGF in AGHM, but free-form bFGFs (FF), improved the collateral circulation to an infarcted area of a coronary artery occlusion in dogs (CAOD).
bFGF-AGHM treatment improves collateral blood flow in the ischemic myocardium of dogs with chronic coronary occlusion.
bFGF-AGHM, but not bFGF, improved the collateral circulation in a canine model with a 2-wk LAD occlusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of a new drug delivery system, acidic gelatin hydrogels microspheres (GelMA) impregnated with basic fibroblast grow factor (bFGFF) in a canine model of myocardial infarction (MI) to improve myocardial blood flow (MBF).
the development of a new drug delivery system for the treatment of myocardial infarction.
the development of an intramyocardial delivery system to enhance the collateral circulation to an infarct area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study demonstrated that the bFGF-AGHM treatment improved the regional myocardial perfusion and the coronary angiographic score in the infarction region of a coronary occluded heart, and that the improvement of regional myocardial perfusions was associated with the increased vascular density in the infarced region.
bFGF-AGHM, but not bFGF alone, enhances collateral development to infarct area.
the intramyocardial delivery, but not the intracoronary delivery, of bFGF in the infarction area is a useful method to enhance the collateral circulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bFGF is a potent angiogenic agent and the delivery system of AGHM is useful in the treatment of ischemic myocardium.
the bFGF-AGHM treatment is an attractive strategy to promote collateral development to the ischemic area of the infarcted myocardium.
the bFGF-AGHM is useful to promote angiogenesis in a myocardial infarction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intramyocardial delivery is a feasible and promising strategy for the treatment of chronic myocardial infarction.
the use of bFGF impregnated in AGHM may be a useful strategy to promote the formation of new vessels and enhance collateral circulation in patients with ischemic heart disease.
intramyocardial delivery is an effective method of delivering bFGF to the ischemic region and that bFGF-AGHM can be used as a novel therapeutic agent for ischemic heart disease.
